+async def test_remove_instance_concurrent_same_instance_htmx_second_redirects(multi_instance_app):
+    """Two concurrent htmx removals of the same instance: both answer with the
+    success redirect, the instance is removed once and its client is closed
+    exactly once (WR-02b).

+    lock = multi_instance_app.state.search_lock
+    await lock.acquire()
+
+    async with httpx.AsyncClient(
+        transport=ASGITransport(app=multi_instance_app), base_url="http://test"
+    ) as ac:
+        hx = {"HX-Request": "true"}
+        task_a = asyncio.create_task(ac.post("/api/instance/remove/radarr/4K", headers=hx))
+        task_b = asyncio.create_task(ac.post("/api/instance/remove/radarr/4K", headers=hx))
+
+        for _ in range(200):
+            if len(getattr(lock, "_waiters", None) or ()) == 2:
+                break

+        assert len(getattr(lock, "_waiters", None) or ()) == 2, (
+            "both removal requests must be queued on search_lock before it is released"

+        lock.release()

+def _describe_json_kind(data: object) -> str:
+    """Describe a parsed JSON value's kind in plain words, for warnings (D-10).
+
+    Never includes the value itself -- only its type.
+    """
+    if isinstance(data, bool):

+    if isinstance(data, (int, float)):

+    if isinstance(data, str):
+        return "a string"
+    if isinstance(data, list):

+def _recover_from_bad_state_file(state_path: Path, found: str) -> TriggarrState:
+    """Reset to default state after a broken state file, logging one D-10 warning.
+
+    Shared by both broken-file cases (D-09): a non-object JSON root and content
+    that could not be parsed as JSON at all. Never reads or logs the file's
+    contents -- only the path and a description of what was found.
+
+    Before resetting, sets the bad file aside as a single diagnostic copy next
+    to the original (D-08): copies to a temp file in the same directory via
+    shutil.copy2 (preserves mode bits, so the copy is never wider than the
+    source), then os.replace onto one fixed name, overwriting any previous
+    copy rather than accumulating. If any step fails, the failure is logged
+    and recovery continues regardless -- the copy step must never block
+    startup (D-11).
+    """
+    set_aside = state_path.with_name(state_path.name + ".corrupt")
+    copy_succeeded = False
+    tmp: str | None = None
+    try:
+        fd, tmp = tempfile.mkstemp(dir=state_path.parent, prefix=state_path.name + ".corrupt.", suffix=".tmp")
+        os.close(fd)
+        shutil.copy2(state_path, tmp)
+        os.replace(tmp, set_aside)
+        tmp = None
+        copy_succeeded = True
+    except OSError as exc:
+        logger.warning(
+            "Could not set aside the bad state file {path}: {exc}",
+            path=state_path,
+            exc=f"{type(exc).__name__}: {exc}",
+        )
+    finally:
+        if tmp is not None:
+            try:
+                os.unlink(tmp)
+            except FileNotFoundError:
+                pass
+            except OSError as cleanup_exc:
+                logger.warning(
+                    "Could not clean up temp file {tmp} after set-aside failure: {exc}",
+                    tmp=tmp,
+                    exc=cleanup_exc,
+                )
+
+    extra = f" A copy was kept at {set_aside} for diagnosis." if copy_succeeded else ""
+    logger.warning(
+        "State file {path} held {found} where a JSON object was expected; queue progress "
+        "and last-run times were reset to defaults (search history is unaffected).{extra}",
+        path=state_path,
+        found=found,
+        extra=extra,
+    )
+    return _default_state()
+
+
+def _start_with_defaults_for_unreadable_state_file(state_path: Path, exc: OSError) -> TriggarrState:
+    """Return default state when the state file could not be opened or read.
+
+    Distinct from _recover_from_bad_state_file: nothing is known about the
+    file's content here (it may be intact), so the warning names the access
+    failure instead of describing bad content, and no set-aside copy is
+    attempted -- the copy would need the same read that just failed. Startup
+    behavior is unchanged: Triggarr continues with defaults and never crashes.
+    The message carries only the path and the system reason, never contents.
+    """
+    logger.warning(
+        "State file {path} could not be opened or read ({reason}); starting with default "
+        "queue progress and last-run times (search history is unaffected). The file was "
+        "left as it is and no copy was made; the next state save will replace it.",
+        path=state_path,
+        reason=f"{type(exc).__name__}: {exc}",
+    )
+    return _default_state()

+<threat_model>
+## Trust Boundaries
+
+| Boundary | Description |
+|----------|-------------|
+| browser -> POST /api/instance/remove/{app}/{instance} | instance_name is user-controlled path input (length-capped at 64, must exist in settings) |
+| concurrent requests -> shared app.state.settings | two settings-changing requests can interleave around search_lock |
+| route -> filesystem (triggarr.toml) | write can fail with OSError carrying paths and system text |
+| route -> log sink | exception text and instance names reach logs |
+
+## STRIDE Threat Register
+
+| Threat ID | Category | Component | Disposition | Mitigation Plan |
+|-----------|----------|-----------|-------------|-----------------|
+| T-87-01 | Information Disclosure | remove_instance failure response | mitigate | Response body is the fixed D-05 sentence built only from html.escape(instance_name); never includes exc, path or exception type; test_remove_instance_write_failure_no_internal_detail asserts absence of "OSError", the error text and the config path |
+| T-87-02 | Tampering (reflected markup) | remove_instance failure response | mitigate | html.escape on the instance name; test_remove_instance_write_failure_escapes_name asserts `<b>` and no raw `<b>` |
+| T-87-03 | Tampering (state integrity) | remove_instance ordering | mitigate | Live settings replaced only after _atomic_toml_write returns; full-postcondition test (D-03) |
+| T-87-03b | Tampering (lost update / resurrected instance) | remove_instance concurrency | mitigate | Settings read and existence re-check moved inside search_lock; lock-held concurrency tests for different and same instance |
+| T-87-04 | Information Disclosure | new logger.error lines | mitigate | loguru only, through the existing redacting sink (triggarr/logging.py); messages name app, instance, config path and exception text, never API keys or SecretStr values |
+| T-87-04b | Repudiation (missing/duplicated audit trail) | writer + route logging | mitigate | log_failure=False only for remove_instance, which logs one contextual error; default True keeps every other caller's log line; real-writer test asserts exactly one ERROR record |
+| T-87-05 | Denial of Service | post-save cleanup | mitigate | Each fallible cleanup step isolated in try/except Exception with logging so one failure cannot leave scheduler job or client behind (D-16) |
+| T-87-06 | Spoofing (CSP nonce reuse) | htmx failure path | accept | Failure path swaps plain text into a row slot, not a page body; success path keeps HX-Redirect (SEC-01) unchanged |
+</threat_model>

@pytest.mark.parametrize("hx_header", [None, "true"], ids=["plain", "htmx"])
def test_remove_instance_write_failure_keeps_live_state(multi_instance_app, hx_header):
    """A failed settings write during removal leaves live settings, the
    scheduler job, the client registry, the state entry and the tag-cache
    entry exactly as before the attempt (D-02, D-03).
    """
    import time

    multi_instance_app.state.tag_cache[("radarr", "4K")] = ([], time.monotonic())
    original_4k = multi_instance_app.state.settings.radarr["4K"]

    headers = {"HX-Request": hx_header} if hx_header else {}
    with (
        TestClient(multi_instance_app, raise_server_exceptions=False) as tc,
        patch("triggarr.web.routes._atomic_toml_write", side_effect=OSError("disk full")),
    ):
        tc.post(
            "/api/instance/remove/radarr/4K",
            headers=headers,
            follow_redirects=False,
        )

    assert "4K" in multi_instance_app.state.settings.radarr
    assert multi_instance_app.state.settings.radarr["4K"] is original_4k
    multi_instance_app.state.scheduler.remove_job.assert_not_called()
    assert "4K" in multi_instance_app.state.radarr_clients
    multi_instance_app.state.radarr_clients["4K"].close.assert_not_awaited()
    assert "4K" in multi_instance_app.state.triggarr_state["radarr"]
    assert ("radarr", "4K") in multi_instance_app.state.tag_cache


async def test_remove_instance_concurrent_removals_both_persist(multi_instance_app):
    """Two concurrent removals of different instances both remain removed,
    live and on disk -- neither request's stale snapshot resurrects the
    other's removed instance (D-02, T-87-03b).
    """
    import tomllib

    settings = multi_instance_app.state.settings
    settings.radarr["Extra"] = InstanceConfig(
        url="http://radarr-extra:7878",
        api_key="radarr-extra-key",
        enabled=True,
    )
    multi_instance_app.state.radarr_clients["Extra"] = MagicMock(close=AsyncMock())
    multi_instance_app.state.triggarr_state["radarr"]["Extra"] = {"last_run": None, "connected": True}

    lock = multi_instance_app.state.search_lock
    await lock.acquire()

    async with httpx.AsyncClient(
        transport=ASGITransport(app=multi_instance_app), base_url="http://test"
    ) as ac:
        task_4k = asyncio.create_task(ac.post("/api/instance/remove/radarr/4K"))
        task_extra = asyncio.create_task(ac.post("/api/instance/remove/radarr/Extra"))

        for _ in range(200):
            if len(getattr(lock, "_waiters", None) or ()) == 2:
                break
            await asyncio.sleep(0)
        assert len(getattr(lock, "_waiters", None) or ()) == 2, (
            "both removal requests must be queued on search_lock before it is released"
        )

        lock.release()
        response_4k, response_extra = await asyncio.gather(task_4k, task_extra)

    assert response_4k.status_code == 303
    assert response_extra.status_code == 303
    assert "4K" not in multi_instance_app.state.settings.radarr
    assert "Extra" not in multi_instance_app.state.settings.radarr
    assert "Default" in multi_instance_app.state.settings.radarr

    on_disk = tomllib.loads(multi_instance_app.state.config_path.read_text())
    assert "4K" not in on_disk["radarr"]
    assert "Extra" not in on_disk["radarr"]
    assert "Default" in on_disk["radarr"]


async def test_remove_instance_concurrent_same_instance_second_is_not_found(multi_instance_app):
    """Two concurrent removals of the same instance: one succeeds, the other
    gets the existing not-found 400, and the client is closed exactly once.
    """
    client_4k = multi_instance_app.state.radarr_clients["4K"]
    lock = multi_instance_app.state.search_lock
    await lock.acquire()

    async with httpx.AsyncClient(
        transport=ASGITransport(app=multi_instance_app), base_url="http://test"
    ) as ac:
        task_a = asyncio.create_task(ac.post("/api/instance/remove/radarr/4K"))
        task_b = asyncio.create_task(ac.post("/api/instance/remove/radarr/4K"))

        for _ in range(200):
            if len(getattr(lock, "_waiters", None) or ()) == 2:
                break
            await asyncio.sleep(0)
        assert len(getattr(lock, "_waiters", None) or ()) == 2, (
            "both removal requests must be queued on search_lock before it is released"
        )

        lock.release()
        response_a, response_b = await asyncio.gather(task_a, task_b)

    statuses = sorted([response_a.status_code, response_b.status_code])
    assert statuses == [303, 400]
    not_found_response = response_a if response_a.status_code == 400 else response_b
    assert "Instance '4K' not found" in not_found_response.text
    assert client_4k.close.await_count == 1


def test_remove_instance_real_write_failure_logs_one_error(multi_instance_app):
    """A failed real write during removal logs exactly one error-level entry,
    naming the app, the instance and the system reason; the writer's own
    "Config write failed" line is suppressed for this caller (D-07).
    """
    config_path = multi_instance_app.state.config_path
    pre_existing = b"placeholder"
    config_path.write_bytes(pre_existing)

    records: list = []
    handler_id = logger.add(lambda m: records.append(m.record), level="ERROR")
    try:
        with (
            TestClient(multi_instance_app, raise_server_exceptions=False) as tc,
            patch(
                "triggarr.config.os.replace",
                side_effect=OSError(errno.ENOSPC, "No space left on device"),
            ),
        ):
            tc.post(
                "/api/instance/remove/radarr/4K",
                headers={"HX-Request": "true"},
                follow_redirects=False,
            )
    finally:
        logger.remove(handler_id)

    assert len(records) == 1
    message = records[0]["message"]
    assert "radarr" in message
    assert "4K" in message
    assert "No space left on device" in message
    assert not any("Config write failed" in r["message"] for r in records)
    assert "4K" in multi_instance_app.state.settings.radarr

    remaining_tmp = list(config_path.parent.glob("*.tmp"))
    assert remaining_tmp == []
    assert config_path.read_bytes() == pre_existing

<objective>
Make instance removal safe against a failed settings write and against a concurrent removal, and give the server side of the user-facing failure message.

Feature: `remove_instance` (triggarr/web/routes.py) currently deletes the instance from the live settings dict before writing the file, so a failed write leaves live settings, the scheduler job and the client registry disagreeing. <threat_model>
## Trust Boundaries

| Boundary | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| browser -> POST /api/instance/remove/{app}/{instance} | instance_name is user-controlled path input (length-capped at 64, must exist in settings) |
| concurrent requests -> shared app.state.settings | two settings-changing requests can interleave around search_lock |
| route -> filesystem (triggarr.toml) | write can fail with OSError carrying paths and system text |
| route -> log sink | exception text and instance names reach logs |

## STRIDE Threat Register

| Threat ID | Category | Component | Disposition | Mitigation Plan |
|-----------|----------|-----------|-------------|-----------------|
| T-87-01 | Information Disclosure | remove_instance failure response | mitigate | Response body is the fixed D-05 sentence built only from html.escape(instance_name); never includes exc, path or exception type; test_remove_instance_write_failure_no_internal_detail asserts absence of "OSError", the error text and the config path |
| T-87-02 | Tampering (reflected markup) | remove_instance failure response | mitigate | html.escape on the instance name; test_remove_instance_write_failure_escapes_name asserts `<b>` and no raw `<b>` |
| T-87-03 | Tampering (state integrity) | remove_instance ordering | mitigate | Live settings replaced only after _atomic_toml_write returns; full-postcondition test (D-03) |
| T-87-03b | Tampering (lost update / resurrected instance) | remove_instance concurrency | mitigate | Settings read and existence re-check moved inside search_lock; lock-held concurrency tests for different and same instance |
| T-87-04 | Information Disclosure | new logger.error lines | mitigate | loguru only, through the existing redacting sink (triggarr/logging.py); messages name app, instance, config path and exception text, never API keys or SecretStr values |
| T-87-04b | Repudiation (missing/duplicated audit trail) | writer + route logging | mitigate | log_failure=False only for remove_instance, which logs one contextual error; default True keeps every other caller's log line; real-writer test asserts exactly one ERROR record |
| T-87-05 | Denial of Service | post-save cleanup | mitigate | Each fallible cleanup step isolated in try/except Exception with logging so one failure cannot leave scheduler job or client behind (D-16) |
| T-87-06 | Spoofing (CSP nonce reuse) | htmx failure path | accept | Failure path swaps plain text into a row slot, not a page body; success path keeps HX-Redirect (SEC-01) unchanged |
</threat_model>

Args:
        request: The incoming FastAPI request (used to access app.state).

    Returns:
        Dict with connected, disconnected, pending, and total counts.
    """
    settings = request.app.state.settings
    state = request.app.state.triggarr_state
    connected = 0
    disconnected = 0
    pending = 0

    for app_name in APP_TYPES:
        for inst_name in settings.get_enabled_instances(app_name):
            ist = state.get(app_name, {}).get(inst_name, {})
            conn = ist.get("connected")
            if conn is True:
                connected += 1
            elif conn is False:
                disconnected += 1
            else:
                pending += 1

    return {
        "connected": connected,
        "disconnected": disconnected,
        "pending": pending,
        "total": connected + disconnected + pending,
    }


def _build_all_instances(settings: SettingsModel) -> list[dict]:
    """Build a list of enabled instances for dropdown filters.

    Args:
        settings: Application settings.

    Returns:
        List of dicts with value and label keys for each enabled instance.
    """
    instances: list[dict] = []
    for app_name in APP_TYPES:
        for inst_name in settings.get_enabled_instances(app_name):
            instances.append({
                "value": f"{app_name}/{inst_name}",
                "label": f"{app_name.title()} / {inst_name}",
            })
    return instances

def _split_filter_param(value: str | None) -> list[str] | None:
    """Split a comma-separated query param into a list, or None if empty.

    Args:
        value: Raw query param string (e.g. "Radarr,Sonarr").

@router.post("/api/instance/add", response_model=None)
async def add_instance(request: Request) -> HTMLResponse | RedirectResponse:
    """Add a new instance for an app type with default settings.

    Validates the instance name, enforces the max-5-per-app limit,
    and rejects duplicate names.  On success, writes updated config
    to TOML and redirects to the settings page.
    """
    form = await request.form()
    app_name = form.get("app_name", "").strip()
    instance_name = form.get("instance_name", "").strip()

    if app_name not in APP_TYPES:
        return HTMLResponse("Invalid app type", status_code=400)

    valid, err = validate_instance_name(instance_name)
    if not valid:
        return HTMLResponse(err, status_code=400)

    settings = request.app.state.settings
    instances = getattr(settings, app_name)

    if instance_name in instances:
        return HTMLResponse(f"Instance '{html.escape(instance_name)}' already exists", status_code=400)
    if len(instances) >= 5:
        return HTMLResponse("Maximum 5 instances per app type", status_code=400)

    # Build new config dict, add instance, and validate before mutating live state
    config_path = request.app.state.config_path
    config_dict = _settings_to_dict(settings)
    config_dict[app_name][instance_name] = InstanceConfig().model_dump()
    config_dict[app_name][instance_name]["api_key"] = ""
    config_dict[app_name][instance_name]["id"] = new_instance_id()
    try:
        new_settings = SettingsModel(**config_dict)
    except pydantic.ValidationError as exc:
        logger.warning("Invalid settings rejected on add_instance: {exc}", exc=exc)
        return HTMLResponse("Validation error: invalid configuration", status_code=400)

    # Acquire search_lock to prevent races with in-flight search jobs
    async with request.app.state.search_lock:
        # Serialize from validated model to guarantee SecretStr extraction
        await asyncio.get_running_loop().run_in_executor(
            None, _atomic_toml_write, config_path, _settings_to_dict(new_settings)
        )
        request.app.state.settings = new_settings

        # Create state entry for the new instance
        triggarr_state = request.app.state.triggarr_state
        triggarr_state.setdefault(app_name, {})
        triggarr_state[app_name][instance_name] = _default_instance_state()

    return RedirectResponse(url=request.url_for("settings_page"), status_code=303)

def _atomic_toml_write(path: Path, data: dict, *, log_failure: bool = True) -> None:
    """Write TOML data to a file atomically using tempfile + fsync + rename.

    On failure (e.g. serialization error), the temp file is cleaned up
    so no orphaned files remain on disk. OSError during the write
    (os.replace / fsync) is logged with the config path before re-raise.
    Non-FileNotFoundError OSError during temp cleanup is also logged so
    permission / read-only / no-space failures are observable (SAFETY-04).

    Args:
        path: Destination file path.
        data: TOML-serializable dict.
        log_failure: Whether to log the primary "Config write failed" line
            when the write itself (not the temp-file cleanup) raises
            OSError. A caller that logs the failure itself with richer
            context (e.g. the app and instance involved) passes
            log_failure=False so one failed write yields one error-level
            log entry overall, not two (D-07). Does not affect the
            directory-fsync warning, the temp-cleanup error, or the
            unexpected-error branch, which always log.
    """
    dir_fd = None
    renamed = False
    fd, tmp_path = tempfile.mkstemp(dir=path.parent, suffix=".tmp")
    try:
        with os.fdopen(fd, "wb") as f:
            tomli_w.dump(data, f)
            f.flush()
            os.fsync(f.fileno())
        os.replace(tmp_path, path)
        renamed = True
        # fsync the directory to ensure rename is durable
        dir_fd = os.open(path.parent, os.O_RDONLY)
        os.fsync(dir_fd)
    except OSError as exc:
        if renamed:
            # os.replace already committed the new contents; only the durability
            # fsync on the parent directory failed. Surface as a warning so the
            # caller does not treat a succeeded write as a failure.
            logger.warning(
                "Config written but directory fsync failed: {path} - {exc}",
                path=path,
                exc=exc,
            )
            return
        if log_failure:
            logger.error("Config write failed: {path} - {exc}", path=path, exc=exc)
        try:
            os.unlink(tmp_path)
        except FileNotFoundError:
            pass
        except OSError as cleanup_exc:
            logger.error(
                "Failed to clean up temp file {tmp} during config write: {exc}",
                tmp=tmp_path,
                exc=cleanup_exc,
            )
        raise
    except Exception as exc:
        logger.error(
            "Config write failed (unexpected error): {path} - {exc}",
            path=path,
            exc=exc,
        )
        try:
            os.unlink(tmp_path)
        except FileNotFoundError:
            pass
        except OSError as cleanup_exc:
            logger.error(
                "Failed to clean up temp file {tmp} during config write: {exc}",
                tmp=tmp_path,
                exc=cleanup_exc,
            )
        raise
    finally:
        if dir_fd is not None:
            os.close(dir_fd)

    last_cycle: LastCycleRecord | None
    # ISO timestamp -- last cycle where >=1 search command was accepted; written only by

    last_successful_search: str | None

    unreachable_since: str | None  # ISO timestamp of first failure, None when healthy

"""SAFETY-05 AST audit: every `_atomic_toml_write` reference in routes.py
must be lexically dominated by `async with request.app.state.search_lock:`.

This script is a static check that complements the dynamic test
`tests/test_web.py::test_concurrent_settings_save_serialized`. It runs in
two modes:

  1. As a pytest test via `tests/test_audit_lock_coverage.py` (in-process
     import + call so assertions are captured cleanly).
  2. As a one-shot CLI check the executor or CI can invoke during plan
     verification: `uv run python tests/audit_lock_coverage.py`.

Why AST instead of a line-distance grep: a handler that acquires the lock,
does N lines of unrelated work, then writes the config is correctly locked
but a grep with a fixed line window would mis-count. Conversely, a handler
that briefly exits the `async with` block via an early-return path and then
writes the config is NOT correctly locked but a grep could still pass it.
The AST walk asserts true lexical dominance: at least one ancestor of the
`_atomic_toml_write` reference is an `ast.AsyncWith` whose `context_expr`
resolves to `request.app.state.search_lock` or `app.state.search_lock`.

Note: this script uses plain `print()` to stdout because it must be runnable
outside the loguru-configured app context (e.g., in CI before any Triggarr
import succeeds). This is the one exception to the loguru-only convention
documented in CLAUDE.md -- audit tooling, not production code.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import ast
import sys
from pathlib import Path

# Default target: triggarr/web/routes.py relative to the repo root, which is
# the parent of this file's parent (tests/audit_lock_coverage.py).
_REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
_DEFAULT_ROUTES = _REPO_ROOT / "triggarr" / "web" / "routes.py"


def _build_parent_map(tree: ast.AST) -> dict[int, ast.AST]:
    """Map id(child) -> parent for every node in tree (single pass)."""
    parents: dict[int, ast.AST] = {}
    for parent in ast.walk(tree):
        for child in ast.iter_child_nodes(parent):
            parents[id(child)] = parent
    return parents


def _ancestors(node: ast.AST, parents: dict[int, ast.AST]):
    """Yield each ancestor of *node* walking upward to the module root."""
    cur = parents.get(id(node))
    while cur is not None:
        yield cur
        cur = parents.get(id(cur))


def _is_search_lock_context(expr: ast.expr) -> bool:
    """Return True if *expr* is `request.app.state.search_lock` or
    `app.state.search_lock` (the two forms used in this codebase).
    """
    # request.app.state.search_lock  (the canonical form in routes.py)
    # ast.Attribute(value=ast.Attribute(value=ast.Attribute(value=ast.Name('request'),
    #     attr='app'), attr='state'), attr='search_lock')
    if not isinstance(expr, ast.Attribute) or expr.attr != "search_lock":
        return False
    parent = expr.value
    if not isinstance(parent, ast.Attribute) or parent.attr != "state":
        return False
    grand = parent.value
    if isinstance(grand, ast.Attribute) and grand.attr == "app":
        root = grand.value
        # `request.app.state.search_lock` or (unlikely) `app.app.state.search_lock`.
        return isinstance(root, ast.Name) and root.id in ("request", "app")
    # `app.state.search_lock` shape: grand is the Name('app') directly.
    return isinstance(grand, ast.Name) and grand.id == "app"


def _references_atomic_write(node: ast.AST) -> bool:
    """Return True if *node* is a Name('_atomic_toml_write') or
    Attribute(attr='_atomic_toml_write')."""
    if isinstance(node, ast.Name) and node.id == "_atomic_toml_write":
        return True
    return isinstance(node, ast.Attribute) and node.attr == "_atomic_toml_write"


def audit_lock_coverage(
    routes_path: Path = _DEFAULT_ROUTES,
) -> tuple[int, int, list[int]]:
    """Walk *routes_path*, find every `_atomic_toml_write` reference, and
    verify each is lexically dominated by `async with ... search_lock:`.

    Returns:
        (covered, uncovered_count, uncovered_linenos)
    """
    source = routes_path.read_text()
    tree = ast.parse(source, filename=str(routes_path))
    parents = _build_parent_map(tree)

    covered = 0
    uncovered_linenos: list[int] = []
    seen: set[int] = set()  # dedupe by lineno to avoid double-counting

    for node in ast.walk(tree):
        if not _references_atomic_write(node):
            continue
        # Skip the import binding itself -- it is not a runtime call.
        if isinstance(node, ast.Name) and isinstance(
            parents.get(id(node)), (ast.ImportFrom, ast.Import, ast.alias)
        ):
            continue
        # If the reference is an alias inside an Import/ImportFrom, also skip.
        parent_node = parents.get(id(node))
        if isinstance(parent_node, ast.alias):
            continue
        lineno = getattr(node, "lineno", None)
        if lineno is None or lineno in seen:
            continue
        # Filter out the `from triggarr.config import _atomic_toml_write, ...`
        # line by inspecting the chain of ancestors for ImportFrom.
        is_import = False
        for ancestor in _ancestors(node, parents):
            if isinstance(ancestor, (ast.Import, ast.ImportFrom)):
                is_import = True
                break
            # Stop walking once we hit a function/class -- imports live at
            # module scope so an enclosing function rules out import context.
            if isinstance(ancestor, (ast.FunctionDef, ast.AsyncFunctionDef, ast.ClassDef)):

        if is_import:

"""Loguru logging setup with API key redaction via custom sink.

Uses a custom sink function (not a filter) so that the COMPLETE formatted
output -- including a raised exception's traceback -- is redacted.  A filter only
sees ``record["message"]`` and cannot redact secrets that appear in
stack traces (e.g. httpx exception messages containing API keys).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import sys
from collections.abc import Callable
from typing import IO, Any

from loguru import logger

from triggarr.log_buffer import LogEntry, log_buffer


def _redact(text: str, secrets: list[str]) -> str:
    """Replace every configured secret value with [REDACTED] in text."""
    for secret in secrets:
        if secret:
            text = text.replace(secret, "[REDACTED]")
    return text


def create_redacting_sink(secrets: list[str], stream: IO[str] = sys.stderr) -> Callable[[str], None]:
    """Create a loguru sink that redacts secrets from the full formatted output.

    Unlike a filter (which only sees record["message"]), a custom sink
    receives the COMPLETE formatted string including a raised exception's traceback.
    This ensures API keys that appear in httpx exception messages or
    stack traces are also redacted.

    Args:
        secrets: List of secret values to redact.
        stream: Output stream (defaults to stderr).

    Returns:
        A loguru-compatible sink function.
    """

    def sink(message: Any) -> None:
        text = _redact(str(message), secrets)
        stream.write(text)
        stream.flush()

    return sink

    """Configure loguru with human-readable format and secret redaction.

    Removes the default handler and adds two sinks:

    - A redacting sink writing the full formatted output (including a
      raised exception's traceback) to stderr, for the operator channel
      (e.g. ``docker logs``).
    - A buffer sink feeding the web UI log viewer: entries are always a
      single redacted line -- either a bound "viewer_message" or the plain
      message, plus at most one redacted "<Type>: <first line>" exception
      summary. No raw tracebacks ever reach the buffer.

    - Format: ``2026-02-23 14:30:00 INFO     Connected to Radarr``
    - Configurable log level
    - Automatic redaction of all secret values in messages AND tracebacks

    Args:
        level: Log level string (e.g. "info", "debug", "warning").
        secrets: List of secret values to redact from all log output.
    """
    logger.remove()
    logger.add(
        create_redacting_sink(secrets),
        format="{time:YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss} {level:<8} {message}",
        level=level.upper(),
        colorize=False,  # Custom sink function, not a stream -- no ANSI auto-detect
    )

    logger.add(create_buffer_sink(secrets), level=level.upper(), format="{message}")
